q: After one partition step of quicksort, where is the pivot?
options: At the start of the array
In the middle index of the array
At the end of the array
explain: Everything to its left is ≤ the pivot and everything to its right is greater, so it never needs to move again.

q: What is the worst-case running time of quicksort?
explain: If the pivot is always the smallest or largest element, the recurrence is T(n) = T(n − 1) + n = Θ(n²).

q: With 'last element as pivot', which input triggers quicksort's worst case?
options: An array with all distinct values in random order
explain: On sorted input, the last element is the maximum, so every partition splits off nothing on the right and n − 1 elements on the left.

q: What is quicksort's expected running time with a randomly chosen pivot, on any fixed input?
explain: Randomisation means no particular input is bad. The expected number of comparisons is about 2n ln n ≈ 1.39 n log₂ n.

q: How many comparisons does one Lomuto partition of n elements make?
explain: Each element other than the pivot is compared with the pivot exactly once.

q: Lomuto partition of [10, 80, 30, 90, 40, 50, 70] with pivot 70: what is the result?
explain: The four elements ≤ 70 are swapped to the front in scan order. The pivot then swaps with 80 at index 4, which leaves 90 80 unsorted on the right.

q: Quicksort is a stable sorting algorithm.
explain: False. The long-distance swaps in partitioning can reorder equal keys. Merge sort is stable.

q: How much extra memory does quicksort use on average?
options: O(log n), for the recursion stack
explain: Partitioning is in place. The recursion depth is O(log n) on average, and recursing on the smaller side first keeps it O(log n) even in the worst case.

q: What happens to standard two-way (Lomuto) quicksort on an array where every element is equal?
options: It runs in Θ(n log n)
explain: Every element is ≤ the pivot, so each partition is maximally unbalanced. Three-way partitioning handles equal keys in linear time.

q: Which recurrence describes quicksort's best case?
explain: A median pivot splits evenly, exactly like merge sort: Θ(n log n).
